concerns.label: Security
concerns.sharedGuidance: Treat security as trust-boundary enforcement: report paths that let untrusted input gain authority or expose sensitive data.

standards.guidance: Treat every trust-boundary bypass as a finding even when the happy path is safe.

cr.scope: Report exploitable weaknesses and trust-boundary defects in the changed code. Ignore correctness bugs with no security consequence - another reviewer owns those.
focusAreas: OWASP Top 10: injection (SQL, command, path, log, prompt), broken authentication, insecure deserialization, sensitive data exposure, security misconfiguration, missing access control
Hardcoded secrets, credentials, tokens, or connection strings; secrets written to logs, receipts, or error messages
Trust boundaries: input crossing from an untrusted source without validation, canonicalization, or size bounds
Path confinement: user- or model-supplied paths joined without canonicalize-then-confine; symlink escapes; writes outside a declared allowlist
Command and script execution built from interpolated strings rather than bound argument arrays
Authorization: missing or inconsistent permission checks, privilege escalation via CI/workflow paths, credentials available to code an attacker can influence
Injection carried through data that later becomes instructions - harvested text, ledger entries, plan content, model-authored free text

dr.scope: Report trust-boundary, secrets, and confinement gaps in the plan itself: controls the plan omits, controls it describes in prose where enforcement must be code, and steps that widen an attack surface without a named guard.
focusAreas: Trust boundaries the plan crosses without naming a validation, canonicalization, or confinement step
Controls the plan states as prose expectations where only executable enforcement holds ("the agent will only write under X")
Secrets, tokens, and credential handling: where they come from, who can read them, what runs with them
Path confinement and write-scope: every new writer needs a declared, testable allowlist
Execution surfaces the plan adds - workflows, actions, hooks, generated scripts - and who can influence their inputs
Injection paths: untrusted content that later reaches an instruction position (prompts, skills, agents, harvested notes)
Mitigations claimed for a risk that the mitigation cannot actually observe or enforce

concerns.label: Correctness & Reliability
concerns.sharedGuidance: Trace whether stated inputs and state transitions produce the intended result, including failure and boundary paths.

cr.scope: Report defects that make the code produce a wrong result or fail badly. Ignore style, naming, and pure performance concerns.
focusAreas: Logic errors, inverted conditions, off-by-one, wrong operator, incorrect operation sequencing
Missing or swallowed error handling; failures reported as success; broad catches that hide the cause
Fail-loud expectations violated: a defined error condition that silently defaults instead of throwing
Null or missing-value dereferences, unhandled switch/state cases, empty and single-element collections
Boundary conditions and off-nominal flows: zero, negative, maximum, duplicate, and out-of-order inputs
Concurrency: shared mutable state without synchronization, thread-unsafe collections, lock inversion, race conditions
Async misuse: fire-and-forget where the result matters, missing cancellation propagation, sync-over-async deadlocks
Retries, timeouts, and idempotency: unbounded retries, no timeout, non-idempotent operations retried

dr.scope: Report logic gaps in the plan: steps whose stated outcome does not follow from their inputs, missing failure handling, and ordering that leaves an intermediate state broken.
focusAreas: Steps whose acceptance criteria do not actually prove the behaviour they claim
Failure paths the plan never mentions: what happens when a step half-completes, or a dependency is absent
Ordering hazards: a step that must precede another but is not wired with `[after: X.Y]`
State left inconsistent between steps - a migration split across two commits, a writer changed before its reader
Retry, timeout, idempotency, and resume semantics for anything long-running or interruptible
Concurrency and reentrancy the plan introduces without saying who serializes it
Assumptions asserted rather than verified - "this cannot happen" without a guard

concerns.label: Architecture & Patterns
concerns.sharedGuidance: Evaluate the change against repository architecture, documented patterns, and the responsibilities of each layer.

standards.guidance: Apply repository-documented architecture and design conventions when they govern the reviewed scope.

cr.scope: Report deviations from the loaded design notes and architecture contracts, and structural choices that fight the existing codebase. Ignore local style nits.
focusAreas: Deviations from the patterns documented in the loaded design notes
Violations of a `locked` contract in the architecture-notes tier
New abstractions or types that duplicate an existing one, or conflict with established naming
Inheritance used where composition fits; reflection or dynamic typing where a strongly-typed path exists
Layering: a lower layer reaching into a higher one, a helper that knows about its callers, a cycle introduced
Responsibility placement: logic in an orchestrator that belongs in a script, or prose rules where deterministic code exists
New behaviour that should be gated behind a flag or a declared extension point but is not

dr.scope: Report architectural gaps in the plan: conflicts with locked contracts, abstractions that duplicate existing ones, and decomposition that does not fit the codebase it lands in.
focusAreas: Plan steps that contradict a `locked` architecture contract or a documented design-note pattern
New components that duplicate an existing capability instead of extending it
Responsibility placement: deterministic work assigned to a prompt, or judgment assigned to a script
Layering and dependency direction between the components the plan adds
Extension points and flags the plan should declare but leaves implicit
Decomposition: phases that cannot be executed or reverted independently
Design decisions recorded without the constraint that forced them, so the next plan cannot reason about them

concerns.label: Performance
concerns.sharedGuidance: Focus on material, realistically reachable cost growth rather than speculative micro-optimizations.

cr.scope: Report work that costs materially more time, memory, or I/O than it needs to. Ignore micro-optimizations with no measurable effect.
focusAreas: Hot-path I/O: synchronous or per-item file, network, or process calls inside a loop
N+1 access patterns; repeated full scans where an index or a single batched call exists
Unbounded growth: collections, caches, logs, or receipts that never shed entries
Resource leaks: undisposed disposables, unclosed streams or handles, connection-pool exhaustion
Unnecessary allocations, copies, or serialize/deserialize round-trips on a frequently executed path
Repeated recomputation of a value that is stable for the run
Algorithmic complexity that degrades superlinearly with a realistic input size

dr.scope: Report plan steps whose cost profile is unstated or unbounded: per-item work that scales badly, repeated expensive operations, and missing budgets.
focusAreas: Steps whose cost grows with repository size, plan count, file count, or invocation count without a stated bound
Repeated expensive operations (subprocess launches, full-tree scans, model invocations) inside a per-item loop
Missing budgets: fan-out, batch size, timeout, or credit cost the plan never quantifies
Unbounded accumulation in files the plan writes (ledgers, logs, receipts, indexes)
Caching or memoization the plan assumes but never specifies
Latency-sensitive paths given no target, so a regression is undetectable

concerns.label: Testing & Evidence
concerns.sharedGuidance: Judge whether deterministic evidence can fail when the claimed behavior or invariant is broken.

standards.guidance: Apply repository-owned evidence conventions while requiring every claimed behavior to remain falsifiable.

cr.scope: Report gaps between what the change does and what its tests actually prove. Ignore production-code defects that tests would merely have caught - report the missing proof, not the bug.
focusAreas: Behaviour changed without a test that fails when the change is reverted
Tests asserting incidental snapshots instead of the invariant the code must hold
Assertions that cannot fail: tautologies, over-broad matchers, results captured from the wrong stream
Error and boundary paths left untested while the happy path is covered
Fixture quality: fixtures that encode the implementation rather than the contract, shared mutable fixtures, hidden ordering dependencies
Flaky patterns: real clocks, real network, sleeps, temp-path collisions, dependence on test execution order
Typed evidence markers that do not resolve to a real named test or a real file assertion

dr.scope: Report weak or missing evidence in the plan: requirements whose acceptance criteria cannot fail, untyped markers, and phases that gate on nothing.
focusAreas: Requirements whose acceptance criteria are prose opinions rather than typed, runnable markers
Evidence markers that would pass trivially, or that name a test which does not exist
Phases that close without proving the requirement they claim to satisfy
Risks with a mitigation that no step implements and no marker verifies
Steps that change behaviour with no corresponding test obligation
Verification assigned to a human where a deterministic check is available
Missing negative cases: nothing in the plan proves the new guard actually refuses

concerns.label: Maintainability & Consistency
concerns.sharedGuidance: Prefer one consistent, documented mechanism and report drift that makes future changes unsafe.

cr.scope: Report things that make the code harder to change safely: drift from the surrounding conventions, duplication, and dead weight. Ignore defects another lens owns.
focusAreas: Naming drift: identifiers, files, and sections that do not match how the surrounding code names the same idea
Duplication: identical or near-identical logic in more than three places - name the extraction point
Dead code: unreachable branches, unused variables, fields, parameters, or never-called functions
Commented-out code left behind (as distinct from explanatory comments)
Comments that restate the code, or that contradict what the code now does
File and module organization inconsistent with the established layout
Documentation and design notes left describing the previous behaviour after the change
Style deviation from the surrounding file: formatting, structure, and idiom

dr.scope: Report plan content that will leave the repository inconsistent: undocumented conventions, duplicated mechanisms, and documentation the plan changes but never syncs.
focusAreas: Two mechanisms introduced for one job, or a new mechanism duplicating an existing one
Conventions the plan relies on but never writes down, so the next plan cannot follow them
Design notes and READMEs the plan invalidates without a step to update them
Naming that conflicts with established vocabulary for the same concept
Deletions the plan implies but never schedules, leaving dead files behind
Steps that leave two sources of truth for one fact

concerns.label: Operability & Observability
concerns.sharedGuidance: Evaluate whether failures are visible, diagnosable, recoverable, and safe to retry.

cr.scope: Report changes that are hard to run, diagnose, or undo in the environments they ship to. Ignore defects another lens owns.
focusAreas: Failures that surface without the context needed to diagnose them: no path, no identifier, no cause
Errors swallowed or downgraded to a warning, so a broken run looks green
Missing or unstructured logging on paths an operator has to debug; noisy logging that buries the signal
No receipt, exit code, or machine-readable output where an automated caller needs one
Exit codes and status conventions inconsistent with the rest of the tooling
Irreversible actions with no rollback path, dry-run, or confirmation
Configuration and environment assumptions that fail late and unclearly when unmet
Idempotency: rerunning the same command after a partial failure must be safe and predictable

dr.scope: Report operability gaps in the plan: steps with no diagnosable failure mode, no rollback, or no visible receipt of what happened.
focusAreas: Steps whose failure would be invisible or indistinguishable from success
Missing rollback for anything that mutates shared or external state
No receipt, log, or index recording what a step did, so a later phase cannot verify it
Human handoffs without the Steps/Verify/Rollback detail an operator needs in one pass
Resume semantics after an interrupted run left unspecified
Exit-code and signalling contracts between components the plan wires together
Diagnosability of the new components: what an operator reads when they misbehave
